sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; corporate registry administered by the Registro Público de Panamá)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with hybrid commercial, trust and foundation-law modules; unitary national legal system
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: U.S.–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force since 31 October 2012)
Panama–Singapore Free Trade Agreement (in force since 2006)
Panama–Taiwan Free Trade Agreement (in force since 1 January 2004)

Panama is a party to the OECD/Council of Europe Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters and maintains an active programme of bilateral double taxation conventions (e.g., Spain–Panama DTA signed 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT preventive rules on money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing); Law No. 70 of 31 January 2019 and Executive Decree No. 129 of 17 September 2020 (as amended) (Beneficial Owner Registry administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos); Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations); FATF Recommendations 10–12 and 24–25 implemented through UIF and SSNF regulatory guidance; Public Registry procedural norms for resident agents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) for incorporation executed by the founder and all UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the document's country of origin, or consular legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports of all foundation council members, protectors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport-issuing authority or licensed notary of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified Spanish translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for each material contributor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (where the bank is not a Panamanian regulated entity)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / constitutive resolution and incumbency if the founder or UBO is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry of the corporate founder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all founders, UBOs, council members and protectors against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT, EU Global Sanctions and Human Rights lists, and the Panamanian UIF/SSNF politically-exposed-persons (PEP) registers. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for domestic and foreign PEPs (12 months post-cessation of office), source-of-wealth and anti-bribery checks, and adverse-media review via tier-1 commercial databases. For the low-risk boba-tea franchise licensing model, standard due diligence applies, but all screening results must be archived by the resident agent for five (5) years under Law 23 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — e-Government Online Services portal (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa/); name reservation and certificate issuance performed via the 'Servicios en Línea' module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official name entries are recorded in Spanish or in any other language written in the Latin alphabet, subject to exact toponymy control; non-Latin scripts must be romanized and accompanied by a certified Spanish translation. The PIF designation must include a denominación such as 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or an abbreviation, and each name must be distinctly spelled without phonological or visual similarity to any existing registered entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministerio / Presidencia / Gobierno / Cancillería / Policía / Tribunal / Municipalidad
Cruz Roja / Naciones Unidas / Autoridad del Canal de Panamá
Universidad / Colegio (education terms subject to ministry approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five (5) business days of an official rejection, the resident agent must file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Director General of the Registro Público, attaching the refusal notice, a pre-approval search report, and evidence of distinctiveness. If the reconsideration is dismissed, the applicant may (i) initiate a new name search and re-reservation at no penalty, or (ii) file an administrative appellate claim before the Third Chamber (Contencioso-Administrativo) of the Supreme Court of Justice within fifteen (15) business days of notification. The name reservation window is not suspensive during appeal; in parallel a fresh certificate is normally obtained to avoid registration delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable in pure virtual form for a Panamanian PIF; Law 25 of 1995 requires a physical registered office in Panama. The office may be the resident agent's law-firm address with a dedicated client sub-code, but it must be staffed and able to receive process. A mail-only virtual office without a licensed resident agent and physical file availability does not satisfy substance or AML/KYC custody rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 5% annual probability) for a low-risk franchise-license and supply-chain holding vehicle at inception; the probability rises to approximately 20% upon any triggering event (adverse media, sanctions/SDN hit, rejection of beneficial-owner disclosure, or registry anomaly). SSNF/UIF and Public Registry risk-based inspections are carried out without prior notice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff per reserved name

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff per instrument page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Inscription and filing of the Foundation Act in the Public Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry tariff scaled by the foundation's initial endowment capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial Owner Registry initial notification filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee for UBO registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm / corporate service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office, correspondence handling and file custody — year 1
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark bundled with resident agent retainer

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of June 12, 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law — Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended; Articles 8–13 (foundation charter), Article 25 (public registry inscription), and Articles 36–47 (Foundation Council and governance).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Private Interest Foundations Section (Registro de Fundaciones de Interés Privado).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Carta Fundacional), executed before a Panamanian notary (or as a private deed where permitted) and duly inscribed in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is fixed by Law 25 of 1995; the Foundation must be endowed with an initial patrimony (patrimonio inicial) sufficient to fulfil its purpose and proportionate to the value of the licensed franchise operations. No escrow account is mandatory, but cash endowments should be held in a Panama bank account opened in the Foundation's name, and in-kind endowments must be supported by a sworn valuation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLUTION — The Foundation Council of Boba Tea Global Franchise Foundation resolves: (1) the initial patrimony of USD 100,000 contributed by the founder is accepted and recorded; (2) the registered office is fixed at [Panama City, Republic of Panama]; (3) [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Councilor, each with representation powers for the Foundation under Law No. 25 of 1995; and (4) the Secretary shall record this resolution in the statutory minutes and provide certified copies to the Public Registry and fiscal authorities upon request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Name Approval Office (Oficina de Nombre del Registro Público)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed foundation names in order of preference, including an alternate, for example 'Boba Tea Global Franchise Foundation' or 'Boba Tea Global Franchise Fundación'. The office verifies the requested words against existing companies, foundations, and trademarks and issues a certificate of name reservation valid for 30 days upon payment of the applicable tariff.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport copy of the founder
Registered agent acceptance letter
Power of attorney in favor of the filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or protected words, the filer may submit a written reconsideration to the Public Registry or immediately reserve an alternative name from the submitted list.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Notary Public in Panama, in coordination with the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish, with mandatory provisions including the foundation's name, registered office in Panama, statement of purpose (global franchise licensing, bubble tea brand development, and syrup supply-chain contracting), initial patrimony, Foundation Council members, protector/beneficiary framework, and amendment/dissolution rules. The founder or legal representative executes the charter before a Panamanian notary, who legalizes the instrument for submission to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter draft
Certificate of name reservation
Founder's passport and proof of address
Registered agent's notarial acceptance of appointment
Statement of beneficiaries and protector (if designated)
AML/KYC documentation of the founder and proposed Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Notary identifies a legal deficiency or missing mandatory clause, the founder must execute a corrective addendum and re-execute the charter; the registry will then accept the amended instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Private Interest Foundations Section (Registro de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter with the Public Registry, pay the official state inscription fee, and undergo legal screening against Law 25 of 1995. Upon approval, the Registry issues a Certificado de Inscripción and assigns a foundation registration entry; the foundation acquires legal personality from the date of inscription.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter
Name reservation certificate
Registered agent's acceptance
Receipt of official filing fee
Sworn declaration of the initial patrimony
AML/CFT due diligence documentation of founder and council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'requerimiento' or pre-registration objection, the applicant has 30 days to present corrective documentation or charter amendments. An adverse final decision may be appealed to the Director-General of the Public Registry within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Fiscal Domiciliation and RUC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos – DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the certified registry certificate, obtain the Foundation's RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) for any Panamanian-sourced income associated with franchise royalty and syrup sales; appoint or ratify the fiscal representative; record the first Foundation Council resolution in the statutory minute book; open a corporate bank account for the Foundation; and file the registered charter with DGI. Notify the Ministry of Commerce and Industries of any franchising activity requiring Panama registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter and inscription certificate
RUC application form and DGI fiscal questionnaire
Foundation Council minutes and officers' identification
Proof of registered office address and resident agent certificate
Bank account opening package, if applicable
Sworn statement on source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI rejects the RUC application or the fiscal domicile is challenged, the Foundation must correct the address or officers' details before the Public Registry and resubmit the updated documentation within the statutory period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health of Panama (Ministerio de Salud – MINSA), General Directorate of Health and Food Hygiene, jointly with the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) for franchise and commercial registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Sanitary Operating Permit for Food and Beverage Production (Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento); Food Product Health Registration for syrups and bases (Registro Sanitario de Alimentos); Franchise Operation Registration (Registro de Franquicia) before MICI.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente – MiAMBIENTE), National Directorate of Environmental Compliance and Environmental Impact Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III — Environmental Registration (Ficha Ambiental / Registro Ambiental). No full Environmental Impact Study is required for a small non-hazardous beverage syrup blending and bottling plant; however, the activity must be registered and an environmental compliance commitment must be accepted.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Effluent parameters for food and beverage premises apply: pH 6–9, BOD5 ≤ 150 mg/L, COD ≤ 400 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 150 mg/L, and oil and grease ≤ 20 mg/L, or stricter municipal standards if discharging to public sewer. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from flavor and cleaning operations must be minimized and kept within the Panamanian air-quality regulatory thresholds for industrial sources; all solid waste must be characterized, segregated, and removed by licensed waste carriers with documentation retained in the operating log.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certificate from the Panama Fire Department (Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá) covering extinguishers, exits, and alarm systems; municipal certificate of structural/electrical load and land-use occupancy issued by the Municipality of Panama; and occupational health and safety workplace clearance, including registration of the Joint Health and Safety Committee and accident-risk prevention program with the Ministry of Labor and Workforce Development (MITRADEL).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama; statutory electronic portal: e-Tax (https://etax.mef.gob.pa) and institutional DGI portal (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must appoint a local licensed attorney or registered agent; protocolize the foundation deed in the Registro Público; submit the sworn registration application, constitutional documents, and agent authorization through the DGI e-Tax portal; obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente); if the PIF supplies taxable goods/services in Panama, activate the ITBMS ledger, register for Facturación Electrónica, and obtain the digital invoicing certificate. Annual filing of the PIF fixed tax (currently B/.350.00) and payment via e-Tax are mandatory regardless of foreign-source-only activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panamanian law provides no check-the-box, CFC, or hybrid mismatch elections. The PIF is mandatorily territorial: only Panama-source income is taxed at entity level; foreign-source income is outside DGI reach. The PIF may voluntarily register as an ITBMS withholding/collection agent to preserve input VAT credits and may elect in the foundation charter whether distributions to beneficiaries are accumulated or distributed; such election affects beneficiary-level Panama-source taxation but not the territorial default.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: any person habitually or periodically transferring goods or providing services in Panamanian territory must register and charge ITBMS. A simplified cash-based small-taxpayer regime is available for annual gross income not exceeding B/.36,000.00; Panama-source supply nexus is determined by place of delivery, use, or exploitation of the service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing on the DGI e-Tax platform, phased by taxpayer class starting with Gran Contribuyente and extending to all new RUC holders; invoices and equivalent documents must be issued in XML format with a qualified digital signature, transmitted in real time to DGI for fiscal validation, and returned with an acceptance/stamping code before delivery to the counterparty. API/web-service connectivity, digital certificate lifecycle management, and offline contingency procedures follow the DGI 'Facturación Electrónica' technical standard; issuance outside the mandated electronic channel is unlawful except during approved contingency windows.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under ITBMS applies to (i) exports of goods physically leaving Panamanian customs territory and (ii) services or intangible licensing rendered for use, consumption, or exploitation entirely outside Panama. Franchise royalties, brand licensing fees, and syrup/supply-chain FOB sales by the PA_PIF to foreign franchisees qualify as extraterritorial export service or goods supply when supported by written agreements indicating foreign licensee nexus, off-shore use, and payment received from abroad. Exported tangible goods require physical customs exit; pure offshore services require proof of foreign place-of-use to avoid recharacterization as taxable domestic supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration (electronic filing via SIGA/WISE or DEX) evidencing actual exit of goods
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or equivalent title of transport showing exporting shipper and foreign consignee
Inward Remittance or Foreign-Wire Settlement Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a Panamanian bank account
Commercial invoice, packing list, underlying international franchise/royalty agreement, and certificates of foreign registration or tax domicile of the licensee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI applies literal- and documentary-evidence audits to zero-rating claims. Missing export declarations, transport documents, or bank remittance evidence causes the supply to be recharacterized as domestic taxable at 7%, with assessment of omitted ITBMS plus monthly late-payment charges, statutory fines up to 200% of the evaded tax, cancellation of export tax credit certificates and refunds, prohibition against new invoicing, and criminal tax-fraud liability of the founder, director, or authorized agent under Law 8 of 2010.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate an independent central bank. The Superintendency of Banks of Panama (SBP) is the primary banking regulator; the Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the State under a full dollarization regime using the U.S. dollar as legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. There are no exchange controls, no requirement for central bank authorization for current or capital account transactions, and no restrictions on profit remittance. Banks apply only documentary checks such as tax clearance certificates and AML/KYC due diligence. Dollarization eliminates FX conversion risk for USD, but transactions in non-USD currencies are freely negotiated at market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Because the U.S. dollar is the domestic legal tender, export receipts may be retained or converted without mandatory surrender or conversion ratio requirements. No statutory timeline applies to the holding or repatriation of export proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) without a Panamanian banking license cannot legally take deposits or operate as standalone banks. They may enter through sponsor arrangements with a licensed local bank or by obtaining a funds-transfer service provider license from the SBP. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) may use a foreign EMI for auxiliary payment processing, but tier-1 banks will impose enhanced due diligence and may restrict inter-account clearing flows to licensed onshore banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director or authorized legal representative is generally mandatory for initial KYC at tier-1 commercial banks. Remote onboarding is possible under a controlled framework using notarized and apostilled powers of attorney, certified corporate documents, and video interviews, but most banks require an in-person appearance before a local notary or a banking officer. A trip to Panama City by the foundation's beneficial owner or a designated managing director is strongly advised to accelerate the process and avoid account-opening delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership, nominee directors, or lack of a clear economic substance in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified and apostilled foundation charter, statutory registry extract, apostilled resolution appointing the legal representative, signed UBO declaration under oath, notarized passports of all officers and beneficiaries, proof of physical office in Panama, local registered agent confirmation, and professional reference letters from licensed attorneys or CPAs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound funds originating from high-risk jurisdictions or unexplained third-party remittances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of source-of-funds bank statements, underlying commercial contracts (franchise agreements, supply purchase orders), a notarized affidavit of beneficial owner detailing fund origin, SWIFT payment trail, and certification from a licensed Panamanian counsel confirming no sanctioned persons are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intellectual-property royalty flows to the foundation from franchise licensing operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Franchise license agreement, Royalty calculation methodology and pro-forma invoices, licensing registry certificate (Panamanian or foreign IP office), proof of adequate economic substance in Panama (payroll records, office lease, management meeting minutes), and a tax due-diligence memorandum showing territorial-source treatment of the royalty income.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections shall be routed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the parent or franchise investor to the PIF's USD-denominated operational account at a tier-1 Panamanian bank. Wire instructions must include the beneficiary legal name (PA_PIF, Private Interest Foundation), the bank account number, and an unambiguous payment reference citing the foundation's ID number and the underlying equity subscription or shareholder loan deed. For capital contributions, the sender must state the purpose code corresponding to general capital transfer (e.g., 'C' for financial/capital account). The receiving bank will apply a 24–72 hour compliance hold pending negative-media and source-of-funds screening. A copy of the capital contribution resolution and the duly executed subscription agreement must be pre-delivered to the relationship manager to pre-clear the transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for franchise royalty payments and syrup supply-chain purchases shall be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers or through irrevocable, confirmed commercial letters of credit (L/C) at sight for high-value bulk inventory transactions. USD settlements clear through U.S. correspondent corridors (e.g., Bank of New York Mellon, Citibank N.A., or JPMorgan Chase) on Fedwire/CHIPS rails. All outbound disbursements exceeding statutory thresholds require current tax clearance certificates issued by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), plus standard AML transaction reporting. Payments to suppliers in China, Taiwan, or the United States must reference the underlying purchase order invoice and reflect the trade purpose code; beneficial ownership information of the receiving entity must be verified before release of funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign exchange contracts (deliverable forwards) with licensed Panamanian or international banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for key volatile currencies (e.g., CNY, TWD, KRW) booked with principal-to-principal ISDA agreements
Cross-currency swaps for long-term balance sheet hedging of franchise royalty receivables and supply-chain payables
Vanilla USD/CNH option collars structured through licensed broker-dealers
Onshore and offshore roll-over swaps in accordance with SBP derivative authorization

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Tasa Anual de Fundación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Private Interest Foundation Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of each calendar year without regard to the foundation's anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus 5% monthly interest; failure to pay for six consecutive months may result in administrative suspension and eventual strike-off of the foundation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Resident Agent Appointment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (through the licensed resident agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual franchise tax payment, ordinarily by each 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a resident agent for more than 90 days constitutes a statutory ground for judicial removal of the foundation and may lead to forced liquidation; the Registry may also impose fines after statutory notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Record Confirmation to Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed resident agent (confidential records; not filed with the Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May, or within 30 days of any transfer of foundation interest or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete UBO records expose the Foundation Council to fines under Panamanian anti-money-laundering law and may result in the agent resigning, triggering the 90-day agent removal process

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for Private Interest Foundations under Ley 25 de 1995. An audit becomes mandatory only if the foundation charter or relevant law expressly requires it, if the Foundation Council passes a resolution to commission an independent audit, or if the foundation conducts commercial activities creating tax obligations under Panama's Fiscal Code that demand audited financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by CTCF (Panama Technical Committee on Accounting Standards) or local GAAP where the foundation voluntarily maintains formal books and records; PIFs are not required to publish or file financial statements with the Registro Público

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council must annually confirm to the resident agent that the confidential register of beneficial owners is accurate and up to date. Any share or interest transfer, including changes arising from franchise licensing or royalty arrangements, must be reflected in the register promptly and in any case within 30 days of the event. The register is not filed with the Registro Público but must be made available to Panamanian judicial, tax, or anti-money-laundering authorities upon lawful request
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (confidential UBO register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–8,000 per annum if a voluntary audit is instructed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate applied to the totality of annual taxable income once taxable income exceeds PAB 1,500,000; below that threshold, progressive brackets apply: 10% on the first PAB 30,000, 15% on PAB 30,001-50,000, 20% on PAB 50,001-75,000, and 25% on PAB 75,001-1,500,000. Panama's currency is the Balboa at parity with the US dollar, and all filings are denominated in PAB/USD.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax system: the core incentive is full exemption of foreign-source income, which shelters the global boba tea franchise royalties, syrup export margins, and foreign capital gains of a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) so long as the activities and customers are located abroad. No statutory tax holiday is granted to a PIF for Panamanian-source income, but collections of passive foreign-source income by a properly administered foundation are outside the ISR base; a Colon Free Zone or SEM (Multinational Headquarters) licence could further reduce the onshore branch rate to 5% or 0% respectively, subject to substance conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 120 (Declaración Jurada del Impuesto sobre la Renta for legal persons), filed exclusively through the DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) 'T@-Pán' electronic portal at dgi.gob.pa; the taxpayer must hold an active RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and DV (dígito verificador). Related-party disclosure is made in Formulario 124 (Información de Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas) and, for large taxpayers, Formulario 125 (Informe de Precios de Transferencia), both annexed electronically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return for fiscal year 1 January - 31 December, with advance ISR payments made monthly by large taxpayers ('Pago Directo' regime, 12 monthly instalments) or quarterly by smaller taxpayers; the annual Form 120 remains a single consolidated filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 120 must be filed within 90 days after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer the hard deadline is 31 March of the year immediately following the tax period. No automatic extension exists: a late payment accrues interest from the day following the statutory deadline, and the annual annexes (Form 124/125) fall due on the same date as the principal return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year covered, e.g. 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, identified by the taxpayer in the DGI system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF without Panamanian-source income must still open a DGI file and may record 'Sin Operaciones' for the period, but only after the RUC and resident agent are in order.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alphanumeric taxpayer identification with check digit; this key links the return to the foundation's master record.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident agent obtains the RUC on behalf of the foreign founder; the agent, not the founder, is the responsible party for electronic filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Private Interest Foundation and its official fiscal address in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The domicile must be the registered office maintained by the foundation agent in Panama; a foreign operational address cannot be substituted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Descriptive activity code per the Panamanian CIIU classification, corresponding to ISIC 5610 franchise licensing and supply-chain operations for bubble tea chains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Selecting the correct code is mandatory and drives the TP profile, the advance-payment regime, and the risk rating applied by DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue sourced in Panama: local franchise royalties, syrup sales, and service fees to Panamanian franchisees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only Panamanian-source revenue; foreign-source royalties from franchisees outside Panama are excluded under territoriality and should be disclosed in an annexed reconciliation to defend the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income items, including foreign-source franchise and supply income and foreign capital gains held in the foundation patrimony.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a sourcing memorandum showing the physical location of the franchise assets, licensees, and sales activities; do not commingle exempt revenue with deductible local cost pools.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred to generate Panamanian-source income: local logistics, warehousing, licensing costs, and administrative charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate costs exclusively against the taxable Panamanian base; costs attributable to foreign-source income are disallowed unless an apportionment method is approved by DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductible costs, losses from prior periods (maximum five years), and inflation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a wholly passive PIF with no Panamanian activity, enter zero and document that distributions from the foundation patrimony are capital transfers, not income of the foundation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISR computed at the 25% flat rate or graduated brackets according to the taxable income band declared.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 25% rate must not be applied to foreign-source income; only Panamanian-source net income enters the tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: Anticipos / Pagos Directos y Retenciones
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for monthly advance payments and third-party withholdings, notably the 12.5% withholding deducted by Panamanian licensees on royalties remitted to the foundation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile credits against the annual Form 124 related-party annex; inconsistent credits are a first-order DGI audit flag for non-resident structures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: Impuesto por Pagar / Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax due after credits, or a recognized credit balance for carryforward periods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A dormant PIF claiming a recurring 'Saldo a Favor' without declared income is treated as presumptive tax evasion and triggers automatic verification proceedings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is sanctioned with fines from PAB 100 to PAB 5,000 and a surcharge of 10% on the tax due, plus compensatory interest at 1% per month (0.033% daily) on the unpaid amount; failure to file after DGI notice leads to a presumptive assessment, automatic loss of the five-year loss carryforward, RUC suspension, and for repeated omissions the digital closure of the establishment (clausura) and registry cancellation of the foundation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final dividend withholding on distributions paid out of Panamanian-source income already subject to corporate income tax; 5% final withholding on distributions from untaxed or foreign-source income. Distributions by a Private Interest Foundation are not legally 'dividends' under the Código Fiscal because the PIF is a patrimonial vehicle under Law 25 de 1995, not a corporation; repatriation of foreign-source foundation assets to beneficiaries is thus outside the dividend withholding regime unless the foundation operates a commercial business in Panama.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network is narrow (in force with Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, and the United Kingdom). To invoke reduced withholding under a DTA, the non-resident recipient must: (i) obtain an original Certificado de Residencia Fiscal from the tax authority of the jurisdiction of residence; (ii) submit the DGI's treaty-relief application (Solicitud de Aplicación de Convenio para Evitar la Doble Imposición) with certified copy of the TRC, power of attorney, and underlying commercial agreement; (iii) obtain DGI endorsement before payment so the Panamanian withholding agent can apply the reduced rate; and (iv) demonstrate active economic substance in the residence jurisdiction. Processing takes approximately 20-40 working days, and retroactive claims are disallowed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific IP in Panama are subject to a 12.5% statutory final withholding tax when paid to non-residents; interest paid to foreign creditors on financing deployed in Panama is likewise subject to 12.5%, with a 0% carve-out for loans granted by foreign banks to Panamanian financial institutions or for qualifying export financing. Treaty partners may reduce royalty and interest withholding to 0%-10%, but only after the TRC and substance review described above.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File documentation is triggered when the aggregate annual value of related-party transactions exceeds PAB 250,000 (USD 250,000), and the Formulario 124 declaration must be filed even at nil amounts by any taxpayer with controlled transactions; a Master File is expected for multinational groups consolidated at or above the OECD Action 13 threshold of EUR 750,000,000 in annual group revenue, and the DGI may additionally require a TP study on request for large taxpayers.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain a formal annual ESR filing regime in the style of the Gulf States, but the substance-over-form doctrine is embedded in tax law: Law 25 de 1995 requires every PIF to have a registered agent, a resident foundation council, a Panama registered office, and books that allow verification of the foundation's purpose; DGI audits under Law 76 de 2019 disregard shell foundations that fail these indicators and re-source the international royalty and supply profits as Panamanian income. A PIF that merely holds the global boba tea franchise IP and receives royalties without local administration, local physical activity, or local decision-making will be treated by foreign tax authorities as tax resident elsewhere and by Panama as an artificial arrangement ineligible for territoriality protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately mislabelling Panamanian-source franchise royalties and syrup sales as 'foreign-source' income, filing a false 'Sin Operaciones' return while the foundation receives payments from Panama, understating the RUC-reported revenue, or destroying local accounting records that evidence Panamanian activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative surcharge of 50% to 100% of the under-declared ISR, interest at 1% monthly, and a fine of one to five times the evaded tax under Law 61 de 2012; DGI may also order suspension of the RUC, closure of the commercial establishment for up to 10 days (60 days on repetition), and asset forfeiture in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and the senior director who signed the false return face imprisonment of 2 to 5 years (3 to 8 years when committed through a PIF), joint and several civil liability for the entire tax debt under Article 764-A of the Código Fiscal, preventive travel bans (impedimento de salida), freezing of personal and corporate accounts, and extradition exposure where the evasion is connected to a foreign jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Foundation (Falta de Sustancia Económica)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF with no economic activity in Panama: no local bank account, no locally held books or minutes, a foundation council composed exclusively of the registered agent's staff, and worldwide boba tea franchise royalties flowing through nominee accounts controlled by founders resident in the US, Singapore, or mainland China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the structure by DGI under the substance-over-form doctrine with retroactive ISR assessment at the 25% headline rate on the accumulated royalty and supply margin, application of the 10% or 5% dividend withholding on deemed distributions, plus the 10% surcharge and 1% monthly interest; the Registro Público can cancel the foundation for breach of Law 25 de 1995, and the foundation agent is exposed to fines of PAB 500 to PAB 10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panamanian courts permit piercing the foundation veil to execute judgments against the founder's assets; directors who certified false 'management in Panama' minutes are civilly liable to the foundation's creditors and beneficiaries; the resident agent may be disbarred, and backdated minutes constitute criminal forgery carrying 3 to 6 years of imprisonment.
